observables.name: l_g_fitted
observables.prediction_source: paper Table 1, l_g = 10.7 um / d = 0.8 um
observables.derivation: For POINT particles the profile is exactly n(z) = n0 exp(-z/l_g) -- a Boltzmann distribution in U = kT z/l_g -- so this is a correctness check, not a physical prediction. Excluded volume perturbs it only where phi is not small, which is why the fit window starts at 2 d and the tolerance is 5 % rather than the 0.014 % the non-interacting capability check reached (verify/verify_sedimentation_wall.py).
observables.note: the decay length of the profile, fitted from the slope of ln n(h)

observables.name: Z_dilute_tail
observables.derivation: With n = n0 exp(-z/l_g), the integral of rho above z is exactly l_g rho(z), so Z = 1 identically. Any error in the cumulative sum, the bin width or the l_g used shows up here before it reaches the EOS.
observables.note: Z -> 1 as phi -> 0. Costs nothing and catches a wrong hydrostatic read

observables.name: Z_dev_wmean_vs_CS_eff
observables.derivation: HYPOTHESIS, not a check: the simulation imposes a WCA core and imposes no equation of state at all, so a mismatch is a result about how well a soft core stands in for a hard sphere. The 2 % band is INHERITED from this repository's own prior measurement of the same substitution (-0.32 % at phi ~ 0.10, -0.51 % at phi ~ 0.21 at eps = 1 kT), not invented. phi_eff = phi (d_BH/d)^3 with d_BH/d = 0.9048.
observables.note: Poisson-weighted mean of (Z - CS(phi_eff))/CS over the window, in percent. ★ THE answering quantity of intake/sediment-pmma-3d/goal.yaml

observables.name: Z_dev_wmean_vs_CS_nominal
observables.derivation: CS(phi_eff) and CS(phi_nominal) differ by -17.05 % at the wall of this cell, so the two are separable by this measurement. No prediction is attached: this number IS the discriminator.
observables.note: the same weighted mean WITHOUT the Barker-Henderson mapping. The GAP between this and the line above is what says whether the mapping is required

observables.name: Z_dev_max_vs_CS_eff
observables.note: the LARGEST single-slab deviation. Reported without a verdict on purpose: at 200 frames a slab carries ~2.7 % Poisson error, so the max over ~40 slabs is ~7 % from noise alone. It is here to show the noise floor beside the weighted mean, not to be compared with 2 %

observables.name: Z_at_densest_slab
observables.derivation: One slab, so it carries the full Poisson error (~1/sqrt(counts)); the 8 % tolerance is that error plus room, not a physics claim. Its value is that CS(phi_eff) and CS(phi_nominal) are furthest apart here, so it is where the mapping question is sharpest.
observables.note: the single most discriminating point: phi = 0.1052, phi_eff = 0.0779, 13812 counts. CS(phi_nominal) there is 1.5563, which is the alternative this point separates from

observables.name: D_xy
observables.derivation: x and y are unconfined and periodic, so the lateral MSD is 4 D t with D = D_0 = 1 in these units. ⚠ the VERTICAL MSD saturates at ~l_g^2 and must not be fit (the card's gate table). Excluded volume at phi <~ 0.16 lowers the long-time D by a few percent, hence 10 % rather than 5 %.
observables.note: lateral self-diffusion in reduced units -- the clock, checked against itself

observables.name: phi_wall_measured
observables.note: the highest local volume fraction the profile reached -- how far up the CS curve this run got

observables.name: min_sep_placed
observables.note: closest pair at t=0. Below ~0.8 d the WCA core starts to set dt
